A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WATCH research. Their complete main texts and appendices A–F support reliable comparison of methods, equations, experiments, tables, and figures despite localized typesetting defects in v5.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic, tabular-data, and corrupted-image experiments evaluating adaptation, detection delays, alarms, coverage, runtime, and root-cause analysis.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The weighted p-value computation, X-CTM-triggered adaptation, density-ratio estimation, betting procedures, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. The added bag-sufficiency requirement restricts theoretical validity rather than changing the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic scenarios, MEPS, Bike Sharing, Superconductivity, MNIST-C, and CIFAR-10-C tasks and shifts. v5 Appendix D.1 reproduces existing benign-shift results from v4 Figure 2 rather than adding dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain CTM, PR-ST, PR-CD-online, and PR-CD-50 comparisons and the same ablation alternatives. The new online-compression-model correspondence table is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Splits, corruption mixtures, alarm thresholds, training settings, and evaluation procedures match. The enlarged validation set and 200-point smoothing described in v5 Figure 10 were already documented in v4 Figure 9.

E4.justification: The shift-severity, density-ratio-estimator, and betting-function ablations are retained, together with runtime, corruption-specific, and root-cause analyses. The added counterexample is theoretical, not a new empirical robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same seed/run counts, standard-error reporting, and interval-width interquartile ranges. These include 200 seeds for tabular comparisons, 20 for runtimes, five runs for Figure 3, and ten seeds for aggregate corrupted-image results.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the matched runtime and image-results tables (v4 Tables 2–3; v5 Tables 4–5) are numerically unchanged, and the plotted experimental data are retained. For example, MEPS WCTM detection delay remains 115.8 ± 3.8. The new counterexample supplies theoretical evidence.

T1.justification: v4 Theorem 3.1 asserts independence for arbitrary joint distributions with exact weights; v5 Theorem 3.3 adds the formally defined bag-sufficiency assumption. Appendix B repairs the conditioning and randomized-smoothing arguments, removes reliance on score bijectivity, and adds an exact three-observation counterexample disproving the unrestricted statement.

C1.justification: The central sequential-validity claim is substantially narrowed to bag-sufficient distributions, with an explicit correction notice attached to the introductory contribution statement. The practical claims about adaptation, fast detection, and root-cause diagnosis remain.

C2.justification: New Remarks B.4–B.6 explain how dependence can permit profitable betting under the null despite marginally uniform p-values, why using the p-value filtration does not resolve this, and why the stated covariate-shift null satisfies bag sufficiency. This materially clarifies the guarantees' applicability boundary; Appendix C's existing fixed-calibration caveat remains.

D1.justification: v5 newly states that accompanying code reproduces the counterexample's exact rational calculations (Appendix B.3, footnote 12). The experimental repository information, model and hyperparameter disclosures, and algorithm pseudocode are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands v4's brief online-compression-model mention through Remark 3.4, Appendix A, and Table 2. It connects oracle weights to Vovk (2003)'s backward kernels and discusses the central theorem's relationship to existing conformal-validity theory, while explicitly leaving a formal reduction unresolved. The reference list itself is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 is reorganized to distinguish one-shot validity from sequential independence, with expanded proof explanations and correction notices. v5 also adds an AI-assistance disclosure and revises the Appendix D.1 heading, while retaining the overall narrative and section order.

P2.justification: v4 Figure 2 moves intact to v5 Figure 5, while main-text Figure 2 retains only MEPS. v5 adds two theoretical tables and adjusts captions and figure sizing. The overall design remains similar, but product operators in Appendix C are newly malformed.

improvement.justification: v5 addresses an important flaw in the paper's central theoretical foundation: the unrestricted independence assertion in v4. The explicit restriction, repaired proof, and checkable counterexample substantially improve correctness and transparency without removing empirical evidence. These gains outweigh the localized typesetting deterioration in Appendix C; the practical implementation's previously documented limitations remain.
